estimated_mcu_benchmarks.label: ESTIMATED MCU LATENCY (Cycle-Accurate Analytic Model, Not Host Measurements)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: INT8 F1 within 3 points of FP32 F1
TCN FPR lower than Decision Tree FPR at comparable recall
Pruning setting saves >= 25% sensor reads with F1 drop <= 3 pts
Gate-ranked pruning beats random dropping at equal reads saved
All pytest unit tests pass cleanly

C1.Claim: A tiny quantized Temporal Convolutional Network (~8-12k params, int8) detects sensor anomalies with lower false-positive rate than shallow models and comparable accuracy to larger models.
C1.Evidence: TCN INT8 has 6,486 parameters and a 31.30 KB footprint. INT8 F1 (0.6935) matches FP32 F1 (0.7029, delta 0.0094) with 99.04% agreement across 5 seeds. TCN maintains a low FPR (0.0227 ± 0.0113), while Decision Tree achieves higher raw F1 (0.8637 ± 0.0077) on subtle stuck-at anomalies due to explicit statistical window feature engineering.

C2.Claim: Dynamic feature (sensor) pruning cuts sensor reads substantially with small F1 loss via gate ranking and runtime wakeup.
C2.Evidence: Gate-ranked pruning cuts 25% of sensor reads with F1 = 0.6239, outperforming 25-draw random dropping by +0.0677 F1 (+1.07σ advantage). At 50% reads saved, gate pruning retains +0.0162 advantage, but at 75% reads saved, random subsets score slightly higher (-0.0175 F1). Dynamic streaming simulation achieves 34.47% read reduction and 33.49% energy savings with 0.050 s detection delay.

C3.Claim: The INT8 model fits microcontroller-class budgets (size, params, MACs, latency).
C3.Evidence: Model size is 31.30 KB (fits in STM32/ESP32 Flash). Analytic MACs: 373,040. Host latency is 0.0210 ms (47,588 inf/s). Estimated MCU latency is 5.83 ms on Cortex-M4 @80MHz and 1.55 ms on ESP32 @240MHz, consuming less than 2% of the 320 ms streaming stride budget.

C4.Claim: The system is robust to noise, sensor dropout and drift.
C4.Evidence: The TCN exhibits graceful degradation and significantly outperforms the Decision Tree under moderate noise (sigma=0.2: TCN F1 ~0.63 vs Decision Tree ~0.30) and sensor dropout (rate 0.1-0.4: TCN F1 0.57-0.64 vs Decision Tree ~0.30). However, under severe perturbation (sigma >= 0.8 or drift >= 1.0), performance degrades markedly, with F1 settling at ~0.32 as signal-to-noise ratio collapses.
